description: Path A test for the borromean-quark energy-scale ansatz: compares the counit net difference ε(ΔNF)=h²/2−h against the Markov-trace difference tr_M(ΔNF) of the nucleon single-wrap NF, symbolically exact. Determines whether the per-braid mass tower reproduces the unweighted net at leading order (ansatz derivable) or differs by the Markov weight z (ansatz is a counit structural choice). Derive-or-refute; nothing wired.

data.verdict: PATH A (net = leading-order tr_M mass) REFUTED, scope (a): Δtr_M/Δnet → 1/2 ≠ 1 = z (the Markov weight at q→1). The counit (net) and the Markov trace are genuinely different functionals differing at O(1), NOT a leading-order coincidence — so the borromean-quark energy-scale ansatz Q_β=|Δnet|·E₀ uses the COUNIT ε by structural choice; deriving it requires deriving why the β-decay/binding channel augments (ε) rather than Markov-traces, not an h-expansion of the mass tower. This is the exact Step-6 'unweighted net vs weighted trace' gap, quantified: it is O(1)=z, not O(h).
